about:
![HeadWow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/uposum/headwow/master/assets/icon.svg) # HeadWow **Wowhead's WoW Forever database, inside the game.** Every item, every NPC, who drops what and how often, where to farm it, and what it's worth. [![Latest release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/uposum/headwow?label=release&sort=date)](https://github.com/uposum/headwow/releases/latest) [![Daily release](https://github.com/uposum/headwow/actions/workflows/release.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/uposum/headwow/actions/workflows/release.yml) [![CI](https://github.com/uposum/headwow/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/uposum/headwow/actions/workflows/ci.yml) ![Interface 16001](https://img.shields.io/badge/interface-16001-blue) --- HeadWow bundles a fresh snapshot of [Wowhead's WoW Forever](https://www.wowhead.com/forever/) database (25,000+ items, every NPC that drops, sells or can be skinned for them, with levels and spawn points, and every way to get each item) and puts it a click away: search it, see drop chances, find the best camp to farm an item, rank mobs by what their loot sells for, and pin it all on the world map. A new release with the latest data comes out every day. ## Features **Browse**: search items and NPCs by name or ID, with filters for quality, source, slot, and your character (usable by your class, your armor type, your level, NPCs near your level). The home page has shortcuts, what you looked at lately, and tips. **Item pages**: the game's own tooltip; every way to get the item (dropped by, sold by with price and stock, skinned, pickpocketed, mined, gathered, fished, found in chests and containers, quest rewards, recipes); the vendors nearest you, the best places to farm it and who drops it most often; plus full *Dropped by*, *Where to farm* and *Sold by* tables. *Sold by* lists every vendor with its zone, price and stock, nearest first, the nearest one you can buy from highlighted and vendors hostile to your faction last. Vendor and auction prices in the header. **NPC pages**: level, rank, title and what a kill is worth; a 3D model you can turn; every zone it lives in with its densest camp; its loot table with each drop's chance, average stack and value per kill. **Where to farm**: zones ranked by the drops to expect from one clear of their best *camp*, the densest ~225-yard patch of spawns (a loop you can actually run, not a whole zone), with every NPC that drops the item counted together. **Gold farming**: mobs a few levels (or many) below you, ranked by what their drops sell for, per kill and per camp clear, counting how many of an item drop at a time, and optionally what skinning them gives. Hover a mob to see where the value comes from. **Wishlist**: star the items you're after. Mobs that drop them list them first in their tooltips, can be pinned on the map, and you get a raid warning and a sound when one drops. **World map**: *Show on map* pins every spawn of the mobs that drop an item, ringed by drop chance, with a banner naming the best place to farm. NPC pages pin their own spawns. **Everywhere else**: mob tooltips show their notable drops; item tooltips show who drops them; Alt-click any item (bags, chat, loot) to open it in HeadWow; a minimap button; a page in the game's Settings. ### Better with HeadWow works on its own; these addons make it better when they're installed: | Addon | What it adds | |---|---| | [Questie](https://github.com/Questie/Questie) | Not needed: HeadWow bundles NPC levels and spawn points from Wowhead. For the few NPCs the snapshot has none for, QuestieDB's are used | | [Auctionator](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/auctionator) | AH prices. HeadWow only trusts an item with a steady market: the median of the daily lows, listed on at least half of your scan days in the last two weeks and still listed lately. A one-off listing never counts. | | OpenMap | Pins on its stitched world map, and a toggle in its menu | | EasyFind | HeadWow's drop sources on EasyFind's item pages, NPC portraits in its results, and an extension tile | ## Install 1. Download the zip from the [latest release](https://github.com/uposum/headwow/releases/latest). 2. Extract it into `World of Warcraft/_forever_/Interface/AddOns/`. It holds two folders: `HeadWow` (the addon, items and NPCs) and `HeadWow_Drops` (drop tables, other sources and spawn points, loaded when first needed). 3. Restart the game. Open HeadWow with `/hw`, the minimap button or the addon compartment. To update, do the same with a newer release, replacing both folders. ## Commands | Command | | |---|---| | `/hw [search]` | Open or close HeadWow, or open it with a search | | `/hw gold` | Gold farming | | `/hw wish [item]` | The wishlist, or star / unstar an item | | `/hw map ` | Show where an item drops on the world map | | `/hw map` | Show or hide the tracked item's pins | | `/hw tooltip` | Drop sources in item tooltips on or off | | `/hw minimap` | Minimap button on or off | | `/hw config` | Settings | ## Daily releases ```mermaid flowchart LR A["wow-forever-scraper
daily GitHub Action"] -- "snapshot
(items, drop tables)" --> B[("wow-forever-data
private")] A -- "ping: data-updated" --> C["headwow
Release workflow"] C -- "convert, lint, test,
package" --> D["GitHub release
HeadWow-1.0.0-20261117.zip"] ``` 1. [wow-forever-scraper](https://github.com/uposum/wow-forever-scraper) scrapes Wowhead every day: the item listing, every item's page (all its sources) and the NPC pages (levels, spawn points). A page that can't be read keeps the previous day's data, and a snapshot that shrank or stopped parsing is never committed. 2. It commits the snapshot to the private `wow-forever-data` repo and pings this repo (`repository_dispatch: data-updated`). A check every 6 hours catches a missed ping. 3. The [Release workflow](https://github.com/uposum/headwow/blob/master/.github/workflows/release.yml) compares the snapshot and `VERSION` with the latest release. If either changed, it converts the snapshot to Lua, lints and tests everything, checks that no count shrank against the latest release (`tools/check-release.mjs`), packages both addons and publishes a release. Its notes show the counts and what changed since the last one: new items, NPCs and drop tables, and the addon's own commits. Versions are `VERSION` plus the snapshot's date: `1.0.0-20261117`. A second release on the same day gets `.2`. Bumping `VERSION` on `master` releases right away; *Actions > Release > Run workflow* releases by hand, and its *force* option releases even when nothing changed. The workflow reads the private data repo with a read-only deploy key, stored here as the secret `DATA_DEPLOY_KEY`. The scraper finds this repo through its `ADDON_REPO` secret. ## How the numbers work - **Drop chance**, **kills** and **stacks**: Wowhead's, from players running its client. HeadWow bundles each item's 25 likeliest sources and every other one of 0.05% or more; the *Dropped by* tab says how many smaller ones are left out. - **Levels** and **spawn points**: from each NPC's Wowhead page (QuestieDB's for NPCs the snapshot has none for). - **Camp**: the densest block of a mob's spawn points, 3×3 cells of 75 yards. - **Vendor distance**: in a straight line from you to the vendor's nearest spawn point, so only for vendors on your continent; it updates as you move. Which faction a vendor trades with comes from its Wowhead page. - **Per clear**: drops (or gold) to expect from killing every spawn in the camp once: chance × spawns, summed over the mobs there. - **Per kill (gold)**: each drop's chance × its average stack × its price: the vendor price, or the AH median minus the 5% cut when the item has a steady market. With *Skinning* ticked, the same over what skinning the mob gives. - **Not counted**: coin, kill speed and respawn times, which no data HeadWow has covers. Herb and ore nodes show on item pages, but gathering isn't ranked: the snapshot has no node positions. ## Development Needs Node 20+ and a clone of the data repo next to this one. ```sh npm ci npm run data # convert ../wow-forever-data into HeadWow*/Generated/*.lua npm run check # lint + tests npm run package # dist/HeadWow, dist/HeadWow_Drops and a zip ``` For a dev install, link (or copy) `HeadWow` and `HeadWow_Drops` into the game's `AddOns` folder. Adding or removing files needs a game restart; edits only need `/reload`. **Tests** run without the game (`tests/run.mjs`, Lua in [fengari](https://github.com/fengari-lua/fengari)): - *logic*: the data modules (search filters, camps, where to farm, wishlist, gold values, AH market rules, the bundled levels, spawns and sources) against a tiny snapshot, with hand-checked numbers. - *convert*: `tools/convert.mjs` on a tiny snapshot in the scraper's format, then the generated Lua loaded and checked value by value. - *smoke*: the whole addon, loaded in TOC order into a mock client (`tests/mock/wow.lua`). It opens every view, clicks and hovers every row, card, tab, menu entry and button, runs the slash commands, map pins, tooltips and loot alert, and fails on any Lua error. **Lint** (`tools/lint.mjs`) checks that every Lua file parses as Lua 5.1, that every XML file is well-formed, and that no local function is used above its definition. ### Layout ``` HeadWow/ core addon: items, NPCs and their levels Core.lua namespace, data access, prices, saved variables, slash commands Search.lua item search and filters NPC.lua NPCs: levels and spawns (the snapshot, else QuestieDB), camps, loot, portraits, hover card Farm.lua where to farm an item Wishlist.lua wishlist, notable loot, loot alert GoldFarm.lua gold farming values Vendors.lua who sells an item: faction, distance from you, nearest first Map.lua world map pins and banner (Blizzard's map and OpenMap) Integration.lua item and mob tooltips, Alt-click EasyFind.lua EasyFind integration UI/ the window: shell, Browse / item / NPC pages, Wishlist, Gold farming, shared widgets, settings, minimap button, XML templates HeadWow_Drops/ drop tables, every other source, spawn points; loaded on demand tools/ convert (snapshot -> Lua), lint, package, release notes, release check tests/ logic, convert and smoke tests, the mock client .github/workflows/ CI and the daily release ``` ## Credits Data from [Wowhead](https://www.wowhead.com/forever/), NPC levels and spawn points included; [Questie](https://github.com/Questie/Questie)'s database fills in NPCs the snapshot has none for, when it's installed. HeadWow isn't affiliated with Wowhead or Blizzard Entertainment.

releases.name: HeadWow 1.2.0-20261128
releases.notes:
Built with the Wowhead snapshot of **28 November 2026 (scraped 06:04 UTC)**.

| | Count | Since the last release |
|---|---:|---:|
| Items | 25,669 | no change |
| NPCs | 5,838 | no change |
| Drop tables | 8,363 | no change |
| Items with other sources | 13,090 | no change |
| NPCs with spawn points | 4,515 | −1 |

### Addon changes
None: this release only updates the data.

### Install or update
1. Download **HeadWow-1.2.0-20261128.zip** below.
2. Extract it into `World of Warcraft/_forever_/Interface/AddOns/`. It holds two folders, `HeadWow` and `HeadWow_Drops`; replace the old ones.
3. Restart the game (a `/reload` doesn't pick up new files).
